subject: Interim assurance letter for post-audit window — CypherWorks
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cypherworks.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cypherworks.com
Date: 2026-03-12T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Request: interim assurance for post-report period

Hi Jonas,

Hope you27re well. CypherWorks is finishing our vendor review for an upcoming integration. We have your SOC 2 Type II report for the period ended 2025-12-31 on file (thank you), but our security team requires an interim/bridge letter to cover the period between 2026-01-01 and today (we27re aiming to close procurement by 3/25).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can provide a short bridge/interim assurance letter that: 1) confirms no material changes to the control environment affecting the SOC scope since 2025-12-31, and 2) lists any changes (if applicable) and the compensating controls?

If possible, please include the expected signatory and an estimated turnaround time — we can accept a DocuSign execution. I27ve attached our minimal procurement checklist for reference.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Security Program Manager
CypherWorks

Attachment: CypherWorks_Vendor_Checklist.xlsx (referenced)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cypherworks.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: interim assurance for post-report period

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the note and the checklist. We can provide a bridge/interim assurance letter in most cases. Looping in Laura from Security and Neha from Sales to coordinate scope and sign-off.

Quick answers up front:
- We can confirm whether there have been any material control changes since 2025-12-31 and provide a short letter if there are none or if changes are minor with mitigating controls.
- Typical turnaround is 3-5 business days once Security confirms the controls state and Legal signs the final text. We can do DocuSign.

Laura/Neha: Aisha27s procurement target is 2026-03-25. Can you confirm the list of evidence we should include and whether we are comfortable issuing the bridge for the period 2026-01-01 through 2026-03-17?

Aisha: can you confirm anyone else on your side who needs to sign/receive the letter?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0189

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Draft bridge letter and evidence checklist (internal)

Jonas / Neha / Vivek,

I reviewed the request. Summary: the SOC 2 Type II report (period ended 2025-12-31) covers our control objectives and systems used by CypherWorks. Since the report end date there have been a few low-risk config changes (mainly routine kernel and dependency updates in the serving runtime) that did not alter control intent. No changes to access control, logging, or incident response processes that would be considered "material."

I27ve drafted a short bridge letter that confirms:
- Scope and report reference (Redwood SOC 2 Type II for period 07/01/2025 to 12/31/2025).
- Statement that there have been no material modifications to the control environment relevant to the report as of 2026-03-17.
- A disclosure paragraph noting routine maintenance/patching and links to change log entries for the period.
- A limited disclaimer clarifying that a bridge letter is not a substitute for an attestation report and does not extend the audit scope.

Evidence I recommend attaching or offering on request (minimal set):
1) Change log summary (2026-01-01 to 2026-03-17) - high level entry list.
2) System access review: evidence that role-based access reviews occurred in January 2026.
3) Recent availability/performance metrics for the dedicated region (if they ask).
4) Confirmation of no open incident tickets with security impact for the period.

Attachments: I attached the draft letter (bridge_letter_draft_CypherWorks.docx) and a copy of the SOC report (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20251231.pdf) for the procurement team.

Next steps:
- Legal review for final wording (I27ll sit with them tomorrow).
- If Legal is comfortable, we finalise and send to CypherWorks for DocuSign.

Note: If CypherWorks insists on signed evidence for all items, this could add 1-2 business days. Otherwise I expect we can meet the 3/25 procurement close.

Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
